tossups.text: In quantum field theories the difference between the vacuum state energy and the next-highest state energy is this quantity's "gap." In nuclear physics, the binding energy is equivalent to the so-called defect in this quantity. In the matrix for the seesaw mechanism, both Dirac and Majorana terms for this quantity exist; that mechanism imparts this quantity to neutrinos. The continuity equation describes the conservation of this quantity in fluids. The Compton wavelength varies between particles as one over this quantity. Obtained in the standard model by symmetry breaking of the Higgs field, for 10 points, identify this quantity which when multiplied by the gravitational acceleration yields the weight.

Its power was initially quite limited, as the governor could veto any of its legislation and it had no override power. Two members were elected from each county, and it eventually challenged the governor's power, helping to spur the Revolution. For 10 points-name this first legislature in the colonies, established in 1619 in Virginia.

Cole and Vishkin gave a distributed algorithm which runs on one of these objects in "log star" of n time. An algorithm which works on them assigns all values in a string to infinity except the source and then relaxes repeatedly. Laszlo Babai recently claimed to have an algorithm which solves a problem about these structures in quasi-polynomial time. That problem, which is not known to be in either P and NP-complete, is to find whether an isomorphism exists between two of these structures. Iterative deepening improves efficiency when searching these objects, and bipartite ones may be colored with two colors. A greedy algorithm which works on these objects by always choosing the lowest weight is called Dijkstra's algorithm and finds a minimum path on them. These objects may be represented by an adjacency tree or list. For 10 points, name these directed or undirected constructs which consist of a bunch of vertices connected by a bunch of edges.

this structure is essential for adrenal cortex hormones. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this adrenal-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The adrenal is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in adrenal cortex hormones.

tossups.text: In human anatomy, this structure is essential for types of joints. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this synovial-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The synovial is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in types of joints.

tossups.text: In human physiology, this structure is essential for types of joints. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this synovial-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The synovial is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in types of joints.

tossups.text: The nymph Clytie was turned into one of these things after watching Helios cross the sky for nine days without food or drink. After Adonis died from being attacked by a wild boar, one of these things called the anemone was created. One of these things appeared where Narcissus fell in love with his reflection and drowned. The death of Hyacinthus caused the blooming of a type of, for 10 points, what type of plant part with petals?

This man claimed that shipments of quinine to soldiers dying of malaria had been delayed during his feud with Jesse Jones. Westbrook Pegler attacked this man for writing the "Dear Guru" letters to a mystic who developed Living Ethics, Nicholas Roerich. This founder of the Hi-Bred Corn Company gave the "Price of World Victory" speech, which proclaimed the "century of the common man." As Secretary of Agriculture, he pursued the "parity payment" doctrine and paid farmers to slaughter hogs while implementing the Agricultural Adjustment Act. This politician succeeded "Cactus Jack" Garner and ran with Glen Taylor on the Progressive ticket in 1948. For 10 points, name this Iowa native who was succeeded as vice president by Harry Truman after serving as FDR's second vice president.

This character is forced to learn how to whistle to attract bullfnches that live in the bedroom of an eccentric blind woman, who requests that fowls named Phena and Strut are brought to her chambers for daily inspections. In a famous scene this character stumbles on a fock of injured pheasants and breaks all their necks. When her husband returns from Brazil he fnds her staying at a fashionable lodging called "The Herons," and earlier the family horse Prince was impaled by the mail carriage when she fell asleep at the helm. A fag indicating her execution is raised at the end of the novel while her sister Liza-Lu watches, and earlier she recited the wrong passage while baptizing her child Sorrow. This character works as a dairymaid at Talbothays Dairy where she meets the husband who abandons her on their wedding night when she reveals she was raped by Alec. For 10 points, name this title character of a Thomas Hardy novel who loves Angel Clare.

This location contains the Fields of Asphodel, and one of this land's judges, Rhadamanthus, ruled the region of Elysium in this land. Tantalus was unable to reach food or water in this location, which contains a descent into Tartarus. Eating part of a pomegranate forces Persephone to stay in this location for part of every year. For ten points, name this Greek underworld ruled by a namesake death god.

This scientist told Stalin that he was ashamed to be a Russian and told Lenin that he wouldn't "sacrifice a frog's hind legs" to the regime. This physiologist removed the esophagus from one of his subjects to study digestive secretions in an experiment that led to his receiving the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. This man financed his lab by selling thousands of containers of canine gastric juice as a remedy for dyspepsia. A mistranslation of the word zvonok as "bell" instead of "buzzer" causes a common misconception about this scientist. For 10 points, name this psychologist whose work with dogs led to his theories in classical conditioning.

One of these texts describes how to awaken the compassionate Avalokiteshvara through meditation, a process called Prajnaparamita. Many of these texts begin with the phrase "Thus have I heard," including one that is framed as Subhuti's question being answered by the Buddha. That text is also called the Vajra Cutter. Another one of these texts important to the Tendai and Nichiren schools is titled after a flower. For 10 points, name these texts central to Hinduism and Buddhism that include the Heart, Diamond, and Lotus ones, as well as one about sexuality named for Kama.

This figure's cloak is described in an ekphrasis ("EK-frah-sis") by Apollonius of Rhodes. While crossing the Anauros ("ah-NOW-ros") River, this figure lost a sandal before entering Pelias' ("PEH-lee-as") kingdom. This figure was engaged to Creusa ("kroy-OO-sah"), who was killed by a cursed dress. In Colchis ("KOL-kiss"), this figure retrieved an object hanging from a tree next to a dragon put to sleep by his wife Medea. For 10 points, name this hero who led the Argonauts on the quest for the Golden Fleece.

Babinet's principle allows this phenomenon to determine the size and shape of small objects. Under the Bragg condition, x-rays experience this effect to show crystal structure. This type of grating produces light and dark fringe patterns similar to Young's double-slit experiment, which confirmed this phenomenon for light. Huygens' [HOY-ghen's] principle, applied to sound waves, explains why this effect makes hearing around corners possible. For 10 points, name this phenomenon in which waves bend around an obstacle.

This city, whose university was often called the "Leucorea" ("loo-koh-RAY-uh"), had its castle library maintained by the chaplain George Spalatin. A group of 12 nuns fled to this city after being smuggled from a convent in barrels usually used to transport herring. To support her family, a woman raised livestock and ran a brewery out of this city's converted "Black Cloister." A pastor in this city was dubbed "Doctor Pomeranus" but was really named Johannes Bugenhagen ("yo-HAHN-niss boo-ghin-HAH-ghin"). The three "Zwickau ("TSVIK-ow") Prophets" sparked a dispute in this city, where Katharina von Bora got married. This city's All Saints' Church housed the grave of Frederick the Wise of Saxony. A document promulgated in this city condemned the theory that "as soon as a coin in the coffer rings, the soul from purgatory springs" advanced by Johann Tetzel. For 10 points, name this city where Martin Luther posted his 95 Theses.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on Lutherstadt until “Luther” is read

tossups.text: A "paradise" of this colour titles a poem in the collection Works and Nights by Alejandra Pizarnik. In The Art of Poetry, Jorge Luis Borges claims that art is an eternity of this colour. Some scholars believe that this colour is used in Don Quixote as a symbol of deception and falsehood. In his poem In the Depth of the Night Silver Water Trembles, Gabriel Celaya describes sleepwalkers who "pass between sheets of ice transparent and [this colour]." An ink of this colour partially titles a poem by Octavio Paz which includes the lines "Never mind the scar, little and luminous: / look up at the sky and its [this colour] tattoo of stars." Apart from directing a poetry journal titled after a horse of this colour, Pablo Neruda wrote an ode to this colour, describing it as the "fingernail of the mountains" and a "river of conceit." This colour is used as a metaphor for death in several poems by Federico García Lorca, who wrote "[this colour], how I love you [this colour]" in Romance sonámbulo. For 10 points, name this colour commonly associated with foliage and plants.

This thinker's metaphor of a tree of philosophy places the "most perfect moral system" on the highest branch. This thinker argued that the material world must exist due to our "great propensity" to believe that it causes our perceptions in a treatise's sixth and final "day." In a namesake "circle," this thinker's ontological proof of God relies on "clear and distinct" perceptions that are only reliable by virtue of him. Princess Elisabeth criticized this thinker's notion of unextended and extended substances, or res cogitans and res extensa, which he distinguished because the former's existence could not be doubted. For 10 points, name this philosopher who wrote the Meditations on First Philosophy, which states "I think, therefore I am."

For the case of 1,3-dienes, homogenous palladium can be used in conjunction with the primary catalyst in this reaction to produce N-substituted imides. An alternative workup for this procedure involves Ing-Manske hydrolysis instead of base catalyzed cleavage and the final step includes a nucleophilic acyl substitution. It begins when potassium hydroxide deprotonates the imide proton of a phthalimide to produce a nucleophile that undergoes an SN2 reaction with an alkyl halide. The resulting N-alkyl phthalimide can be cleaved using hydrazine to produce a dicarboxylic acid. For 10 points, what is this organic reaction used to synthesis primary amines from alkyl halides?

This dynasty captured Gilget Valley under the command of Goguryeo-Korean General Gao Xinzhi, allowing the Silk Road to be reopened. Among the many technological developments during this dynasty's rule were the use of pig thyroids to treat goiters, the world's first clockwork escapement mechanism, and woodblock printing. This dynasty also saw a half-Turk commander establish the rival Yan Dynasty in a revolt that killed over thirty million people, the An Shi Rebellion. Abandoning the nine-rank system of the dynasty that preceded it, this dynasty implemented a civil service examination to draft officials that tested knowledge of Confucian classics and literary abilities. For 10 points, identify this Chinese imperial dynasty that succeeded the Sui dynasty and ruled from 618 to 907 AD.

One battle on this body of water saw the destruction of Phillip VI's fleet at Sluys (sluweese). One attempt to secure control of this body of water for Operation Sea Lion resulted in the Blitz, while another attempt ended with destruction of the French fleet at the Battle of Trafalgar. Name this body of water, crossed before the Battle of Hastings by William the Conqueror, which Hitler and Napoleon failed to cross to invade England.

parts.text: Identify this type of transistor which, unlike a BJT, has electrodes at gate, source, drain, and body contacts, and works by allowing electrons to flow from the source to the drain. They have mostly replaced BJTs in modern electronics due to factors such as their simpler manufacturing process. By far the most common type is the MOS.
When a gate voltage is applied to the FET, one of these develops between the n- and p-type regions. In a pn junction, these regions form when electrons and holes recombine, exposing bound charge.
When designing a transistor amplifier, it is necessary to determine this point, which refers to the DC voltage around which the signal swings.

parts.text: This Argentine-born Marxist helped Fidel Castro to overthrow Fulgencio Batista in the 26th of July Movement. He is the subject of Alberto Korda's photograph "Guerrillero Heroico."
This Lithuanian-born anarchist published the periodical Mother Earth and was the lover of Alexander Berkman, who tried to assassinate Henry Clay Frick during the Homestead Strike.
A trail named for this leader of the Viet Minh was a supply route that he used to fight Ngo Dinh Diem's government. This man commanded the north to victory in the Vietnam War.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these 20th century revolutionaries.

parts.text: In this phenomenon, a crystal splits a single unpolarized ray of light into two plane-polarized light beams whose planes of polarization are perpendicular to each other.
Brewster's law relates the incident angle of an unpolarized ray of light to this quantity for a medium in which the transmitted ray is partially polarized. This quantity is around 1.33 for water.

The square of this trig function is found in Malus' law, which relates the transmitted intensity of a beam of plane-polarized light to the incident intensity. For projectiles, the vertical component of velocity is found using sine, while this trig function is used to find the horizontal component.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the polarization of light, for 10 points each.

parts.text: The daughters of Nyx or Atlas, these three Greek goddesses are the goddesses of the evening and sunset.
This sun God became angry after Odysseus's men ate some of his sacred cattle. He is known for appearing each day in a horse-drawn chariot.
This Titan goddess of the dawn is the sister of Helios and lover of Tithinus, who was turned into a grasshopper after this goddess forgot to ask Zeus to grant him eternal youth.

bonuses.leadin: Identify these gods and goddesses from Greek myth with something in common for 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this Ma·ja·pa·hit king who was served by the prime minister Gajah Mada. This king's desire to marry Citra Rashmi led to the Battle of Bubat.
The Battle of Bubat occurred in Majapahit's capital Trowulan, which was located on this most populous island of Indonesia.
The Reog dance possibly uses this animal as satire of late Majapahit rulers. Dragons and these animals name a "dance" performed on Chinese New Year using a long costume.

acceptableAnswers: Tvorčestvo Fransua Rable i narodnaja kul'tura srednevekov'ja i Renessansa

parts.text: In The Dialogic Imagination, Bakhtin outlined the concepts of heteroglossia, dialogism, and this other concept, referring to the way that temporal and spatial relationships interact in literature.
Bakhtin is from this country. He wrote about one of its authors in Problems of Dostoyevsky's Art.
acceptableAnswers: the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic

This falcon headed god often identified with Atum and Amun was the chief solar deity in Egyptian myth.
Amaterasu is the sun goddess within this belief system, whose adherents believe in gods or spirits known as kami.

parts.text: Name this general term that refers to portion of the ownership of a corporation. They often come in "common" and "preferred" forms, and are traded on a namesake "exchange."

This financial instrument conveys the right to partake in a future transaction. One which conveys the right to buy something is a "call," while one which conveys the right to sell something is a "put".
Shares of these securities are traded in "creation units." Similar to mutual funds but traded like stocks, most of them track indexes such as the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

parts.text: Name this youngest son of Kronos, whose domain is the sky. This Greek God wields the thunderbolt.
Zeus was hidden in a cave on Mount Ida where he was raised by this she-goat. The Cornucopia is sometimes said to have originated from a broken horn belonging to this figure.
According to some sources, Zeus was hung from one of these objects to ensure that he was not in the sea, on land, or in the sky, and thus invisible to Kronos, who ruled over those three domains.

bonuses.leadin: According to Ovid, this god sent an eagle to retrieve the remains of the slain Ophiotaurus and burned them to ensure the Olympians' victory in the Titanomachy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this deity, who is often depicted with a serpent around his neck and a crescent moon on his forehead. This member of the Hindu trimurti often carries a weapon called the Trishula.
This wife of Shiva is sometimes represented as a yoni alongside a lingam. Her incarnations include Kali and Durga.
The child of Parvati and Shiva and brother of Ganesha is this Hindu god of war. His mount is a peacock, and he uses a spear known as the Vel.

parts.text: In 1852 he became the second Jew to serve in the U.S. Senate. He was the CSA's first attorney general, resigned as Secretary of War in 1862 over a quarrel with Stonewall Jackson, and then became CSA Secretary of State.

This law partner of Judah Benjamin had been sent by James K. Polk to Mexico in 1846 to negotiate a treaty making the Rio Grande America's southern border; later, he served as Confederate ambassador to France.
The author of A Constitutional History of the War Between the States, this diminutive Georgian served as Confederate vice president.

Lieutenant Gustl was written by an author from this country. It is also the home of the drama The Jewess of Toledo and of The Loser, a novel about a pianist who becomes obsessed with Glenn Gould.
Arthur Schnitzler, the author of Lieutenant Gustl, wrote of Fridolin's visit to a mask orgy in A Dream Story. Fridolin works in this profession, the same job held by Bernard Rieux and Charles Bovary.

parts.text: Identify this thinker who formulated the "three-stage model" in which mankind goes through a theological, metaphysical, and finally scientific stages.
Comte was the founder of sociology and this school of thought, whose logical branch was later espoused by the Vienna Circle.

This philosopher disagreed with Comte and used Comtian societal terms in normative rather than descriptive ways. His System of Synthetic Philosophy attempted to prove that evolution applied to all disciplines.

parts.text: Its myriad functions include controlling food intake, sex drive, and fight-or-flight reaction. Identify this region of the brain which links the nervous system to the endocrine system by controlling the pituitary gland.
This lobe of the brain contains the primary auditory cortex which receives signals from the cochlea. It also contains the hippocampus and thus plays an important role in memory.
This other region of the brain is located within the basal ganglia; it sends out fibers to tissues on both sides of the brain and is degenerated in Parkinson's disease.

The Ostend Manifesto called for the annexation of Cuba during this man's presidency. This successor of Millard Fillmore signed the Kansas-Nebraska Act of 1854.
John Randolph coined this term to refer to Northern politicians with Southern sympathies. This term applies to Pierce, Buchanan, and Stephen Douglas.

This treaty, put into effect in 1993, transformed the European Economic Community into the EU, devised the euro currency, and established common citizenship rights.

acceptableAnswers: accept European Coal and Steel Community
